title: MG0c: Turing patterning at the predicted wavelength, local_species_reactions@1's first acceptance on resolved_pump_tissue@3's species transport
status: PROPOSED (drafted 14 November 2026 by the D152 engine agent from the development runs named in development_runs, revised the same day after the lead's review with the advisor (review); not registered, and no judged run is made before the lead registers it)
question: Does local_species_reactions@1, composed with @3's species transport on a closed chain, run the declared discrete system: the engine order's own map for linear networks and for Schnakenberg linearised, exact mode propagation and the nonlinear pattern to the scheme's step terms, only admissible modes growing, the predicted dominant mode and growth rate, the staircase of fastest modes against the domain's length, decay below the critical ratio, and closed accounting?
engine_models: resolved_pump_tissue@3 (src/cells/core/surface_pump_v3_spec.py, src/cells/models/surface_pump_v3.py), IMEX ARS(2,2,2), CPU, float64
local_species_reactions@1 (src/cells/models/operators/species_reactions.py): driven mass action; ideal_detailed_balance_mass_action@1 in guard 2's passive world
scope: MG0c's judged arms run local_species_reactions@1's driven mass action only, of orders 0, 1 and 3 (Schnakenberg's four reactions; guard 2's open world and the sites world, orders 0 and 1), at outside nodes, with resolved_pump_tissue@3's species transport on faces in resolved_pump_composite@1, with five species per world (three quiescent ions and the network's two), within the 7 species the scope stays at: D150's cap of 16 since FR-9 / D165 is not exercised. One judged guard world departs from driven mass action, flagged for the lead (question 1): guard 2's passive world runs ideal_detailed_balance_mass_action@1 (A <-> B, linear) at outside nodes, judged against the engine order's exact map. Every other use of the passive law, Michaelis-Menten, Hill factors, cell routes, D150's writers and the mixed-node heat and work split enters only through test files; the heat and work split is guarded, not qualified, until the first mixed-node protocol. A qualified statement from this protocol carries this scope

predictions_at_drafting.note: for orientation only: the judged run recomputes every prediction

rules.dt_study: S5's form, per element and record (D150's protocol): the step term |q(dt) - q(dt/2)| at the same records, the tolerance 3 x (the step term + the reference term), the reference term 64 eps x the scale for an exact reference (the scale the largest |reference| over the item's records), plus the reference's own difference |rtol 1e-12 - rtol 1e-13| for DOP853; judged at 50 and 25 ms
rules.what_the_rule_shows: as D150's review found, the dt-study rule detects bias, not order: for a second-order error the ratio sits at 4/9 by structure, so the rule's power is its judged controls'; the orders are reported, and only their stop rules are judged
rules.orders: per record, log2 of successive max-norm differences |q(dt) - q(dt/2)| / |q(dt/2) - q(dt/4)|, where both lie above 64 eps x the scale; the stop rule: every measurable difference decreases
rules.linearised_map: ruling 3: Q1's engine against the linearised engine-order map within 1e-6 at 50 ms (the development's worst 1.3e-07); its control, the exact propagator, must fail it there (the development's smallest 3.3e-06). At 25 and 12.5 ms the agreement is reported (linearised_map_by_dt), since the smallest discretisation error there (8.2e-07 and 2.1e-07) lies below 1e-6
rules.controls: ruling (c), by parameter: each of k, a, b, D_U and D_V perturbed in the reference by (1 + delta) on Q1's items (the exact propagator with K = k J(a, b) and D, the whole 1-2-5 grid from 1e-14 to 0.5) and on Q6's (the reference re-integrated, bisected on the 1-2-5 grid from 1e-9 to 1e-1). A control is kept when 10 x its smallest caught delta is at most 1e-2 and is registered there; the others are removed with their reasons (controls.removed); every parameter keeps at least one, so each is caught by a judged criterion at a small delta with 10 x margin (Control_k to Control_D_V). Each criterion requires every kept control of its parameter to catch at its registered delta, stricter than the ruling's 'at least one'
rules.controls_evaluable: why the control criteria fail outside a judged run: they read caught_at_registered, which the driver writes only when the registered deltas are loaded, that is under --protocol (a judged run, or a registered dry-run copy). A development run has no registered deltas, so the metric is missing and evaluate fails a missing metric (development_values names them not evaluable). Their passing path has never run for these five criteria (milestone 3's dry run loaded the old k and D_V deltas on Q1's quick part alone), so the rehearsal on main must run them to a pass on a registered dry-run copy before registration
rules.near_ties: ruling 5: Q4's fit tolerance is Q3's 1e-2, relative; the fastest two candidates at a length are a near tie when their gap is below 2 x 1e-2 x the larger |rate|, from the references alone before any run, and such a length is excluded; the sign margin (the smallest |rate| over 1e-2 x the largest) is reported beside it
rules.judged_run: once, after registration, from a fresh clean execution snapshot of main (validation/source_snapshot.py, no dirty patch), through scripts/run_detached.sh. A failure is recorded and diagnosed, never retuned
rules.attempts: an attempt that ends by infrastructure before its verdict is written is not a verdict: an out-of-memory kill, a unit stopped by the slice, a host crash, a harness timeout, a unit killed by its runtime limit (--runtime-max), a part run that ends incomplete (the judge refuses it: results.json's requested parts and complete), or a guard file whose process ends by a signal (judge-guards then writes infrastructure.json, not verdict.json). It is recorded with its logs and partial outputs and rerun once from the same snapshot; each attempt writes its own output directory, since every judged entry refuses an existing one. A second infrastructure ending goes to the lead, as does any other ending without a verdict. A run that has written its verdict is final (S5's rule). A part the engine refuses is a verdict: its criteria fail; a test failure or error inside a completed guards run is a verdict too
rules.timing: each judged unit runs through scripts/run_detached.sh with --oom-first in its own unit, its --runtime-max about 3 x its development seconds plus 10 min (development_runs.timing: development's figures until the rehearsal measures them; judge-guards from the guard files' seconds, uncapped per file; judge and combine, which run nothing, 600 s), q7 with a cap of at least 5 GiB (ruling 9) and unit b likewise (resources). The judged units run without --wait-headroom: the lead launches each only after checking that the slice has room for the unit's development peak plus a margin, so each runtime limit measures the entry alone and no wait can spend the single rerun
rules.resolved_start: every run starts resolved: the uniform state with a mode of 1e-7 c* or seeded noise of 1e-3 c*, never a switch-on from the trace

at_grid_floor.note: each of these is caught at its grid's lowest point, so its threshold lies at or below it and its registered delta is at least 10 x the threshold (measured). Why, inferred from the tolerances, not measured: on Q6, a and b set the uniform state (u* = (a + b) c*, v* = b c* / (a + b)^2), which k and the diffusivities do not, so a change of delta moves every element by order delta c* from the start, while at the early records, where the pattern is still small, the per-element tolerance falls toward the reference term (its smallest 1.3e-14 mM over the records, against elements of order 0.001 mM); the floor catch is consistent with that

q4_near_ties.note: the sign margin is below 1 at L/l = 26.5: a near-marginal candidate's |rate| is under 1e-2 of the fastest one's there. A sign rests on each candidate's own fit, and each length's smallest-|rate| candidate fits its predicted rate to at most 0.00051 relative (L/l = 28, n = 4), so no sign is in doubt and no length is excluded for it
